questions.learningObjective: find the radius of a circle from its diameter
questions.stem: A bicycle wheel is labeled 26 inches for its tire diameter, the distance across the wheel measured through its center. What is the wheel's radius?

options.misconception: believes the tire label already measures the radius
doubles the labeled length instead of halving it
halves twice, treating the label as a diameter of a diameter

questions.explanation: The diameter is the segment running rim to rim through the center, and the radius is exactly half of it: 26 / 2 = 13 inches. Reading the tire label as the radius stops at the hub and leaves the far half of the wheel unmeasured. Doubling to 52 inches builds a segment twice as long as the wheel, and halving twice to 6.5 inches keeps only a quarter of the span.
questions.hint: A diameter crosses the center from rim to rim; a radius runs from the center to the rim.

questions.learningObjective: compute the circumference of a circle from its radius
questions.stem: A walking path circles a round pond of radius 13 feet. How far does a walker travel in one complete lap of that path?

options.misconception: omits the leading factor of 2 in the circumference formula
scales the radius to 26 before applying the formula
drops π entirely and treats the radius as the full lap

questions.explanation: The distance once around a circle is its circumference, C = 2πr, so with r = 13 feet the lap is 2 × π × 13 = 26π feet, about 81.7 feet. Using πr = 13π feet drops the leading 2, which counts only half the trip around the pond. Reaching 52π feet describes a pond of radius 26 feet, and 26 feet discards π, the factor that turns a radius into a distance along the arc.
questions.hint: The distance once around a circle is 2πr.

questions.learningObjective: identify the diameter as the longest possible chord of a circle
questions.stem: A perfectly round pond has radius 6 meters. Three straight wooden planks are laid across it, spanning 12 meters, 10 meters, and 5 meters. What is the greatest length a plank spanning the pond can have, and where does that plank sit?

options.text: 12 meters, on the plank through the center
10 meters, on the plank missing the center
options.misconception: picks the longer off-center chord instead of the diameter

options.text: 6 meters, on a plank ending at the center
options.misconception: reports the radius as if a span could reach the far bank

options.text: 24 meters, on a plank twice the radius
options.misconception: doubles the radius as if the diameter were four radii

questions.explanation: A chord is any segment with both endpoints on the circle, and the diameter is the longest possible chord because it is the one passing through the center: 2 × 6 = 12 meters. A chord that misses the center cuts the circle obliquely, so its span is strictly shorter, which is why the 10-meter and 5-meter planks fall short. Quoting 6 meters stops at the center, and 24 meters would reach past the far bank.
questions.hint: No chord can be longer than the one chord that passes through the center.

options.misconception: confuses a single touching point with a full-width crossing

options.misconception: denies that the fence crosses the water at all

A chord held at a constant offset always falls short of the full span, so a constant distance cannot produce 13 meters. A tangent would touch the shore at one point and enclose no water, and a line outside the water never crosses the pond.

doubles the 12-inch offset as if it were the radius
adds the 13-inch and 12-inch lengths instead of Pythagoras

questions.explanation: Drop a perpendicular from the hub to the chord; it bisects the chord, so the half-chord is a leg of a right triangle whose other leg is the 12-inch offset and whose hypotenuse is the 13-inch radius. That gives half = √(13² − 12²) = √(169 − 144) = √25 = 5, so the chord is 2 × 5 = 10 inches. Reporting 5 inches forgets to double the half-chord, and 26 inches is the diameter, which occurs only when a chord passes through the center.

questions.learningObjective: locate the center using the perpendicular bisector of a chord
questions.stem: On a clock face, twelve hour marks sit 30 degrees apart around the rim, and the segment from the 12 mark to the 6 mark is a chord of the face. What must be true of the clock's center?

options.text: It lies on the perpendicular bisector of that chord
It lies on the chord's own midpoint only
options.misconception: puts the center on the chord, true only for a diameter

options.text: It lies off both the chord and its bisector
options.misconception: denies that the center is on the bisector at all

options.text: It lies on the chord's perpendicular at its endpoint
options.misconception: confuses the bisector with a tangent at an endpoint

questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector of a chord always passes through the circle's center, and that one fact is what makes every diameter and half-chord calculation possible. Sitting only at the midpoint puts the center on the chord itself, which holds for a diameter but not for chords in general. A perpendicular raised at an endpoint is a tangent line instead, and a center off both lines would contradict the theorem outright.

questions.learningObjective: compare the distances from the center to two chords of different lengths
questions.stem: Inside a circle of radius 10 inches, two parallel chords are drawn, one 16 inches long and one 12 inches long. How far from the center does the 16-inch chord sit?

options.text: The 16-inch chord is 6 inches from the center
The 16-inch chord is 8 inches from the center
options.misconception: gives the longer chord the larger offset, the reverse

options.text: The 16-inch chord is 4 inches from the center
options.misconception: subtracts the chord from the radius without bisecting

options.text: The 16-inch chord is 10 inches from the center
options.misconception: sets the offset equal to the radius, as if a diameter

questions.explanation: Perpendiculars from the center to the two chords bisect them, giving right triangles with hypotenuse 10. For the 16-inch chord the half is 8, so the offset is √(10² − 8²) = √(100 − 64) = √36 = 6 inches; for the 12-inch chord the half is 6, so its offset is √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 inches. Longer chords lie nearer the center, so swapping the two values inverts the theorem that equal offsets force equal chords.
questions.hint: Bisect each chord, then use the radius as the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

Splits it into one half and one remainder

options.text: Splits it into four unequal pieces
options.misconception: counts the pieces produced by two cuts, not one

A visitor stands at point C on the curved shoreline between the two banks, and the walk from A to C and from C to B is entirely straight. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle ACB at the visitor's position?

halves twice, placing the vertex at the center
measures the angle off the full 360-degree turn

halves the arc twice, as if the vertex were on it
doubles the arc instead of halving it to reach the center

questions.learningObjective: explain why inscribed angles on the same arc are congruent

Each post sights across the water to the same two bridges, X on the east bank and Y on the west bank, forming an inscribed angle at each post with sides running to X and to Y. What must be true about the two angles?

options.text: They are congruent because both intercept the same arc
They differ by twice the arc's measure
options.misconception: believes the angles scale with the arc's measure

options.text: One equals the other plus 180 degrees
options.misconception: adds a straight angle as if the posts were opposite

options.text: They match only if both posts sit at the center
options.misconception: thinks equal angles need a vertex at the center

questions.explanation: An inscribed angle measures half its intercepted arc, and both posts intercept the identical arc from X to Y running along the far side of the pond, so the two angles are congruent no matter how far apart the posts stand. They are congruent and equal each other

options.misconception: invents a fixed ratio between the two halves
forgets to halve the arcs before adding them

questions.stem: On a standard clock face the minute hand starts at the 12 and returns to the 12 after 60 seconds. Starting from the 12, what is the measure, in degrees, of the arc its tip traces in 20 seconds?

treats twenty seconds as a small slice of a turn
reports a quarter turn, the span of one hour mark

halves the arc fraction twice, behaving as if 30

halves the sum of the arcs a second time
subtracts the arcs as if the vertex lay outside

halves the far arc alone, ignoring the near one
treats the platform as a point on the circle's rim

questions.learningObjective: classify a point as inside, on, or outside using its distance from the center
questions.stem: A circular pond has center C and radius 40 meters. Three lily pads are anchored 25 meters, 40 meters, and 55 meters from C. Which statement classifies all three pads correctly?

options.misconception: counts a shore distance as strictly inside
reverses which distances lie inside and outside
swaps inside and outside for every pad

questions.explanation: Compare each distance with the radius of 40 meters: 25 < 40 places the first pad inside, 40 = 40 places the second exactly on the shore, and 55 > 40 places the third outside. Any answer that swaps these roles inverts the comparison, because a distance greater than the radius always leaves the circle and one smaller than the radius never leaves it.
questions.hint: Compare each distance to the radius: less, equal, greater.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY

questions.learningObjective: build a center-radius equation from the endpoints of a diameter
questions.stem: Two docks on a circular pond sit at the coordinate points (−2, 5) and (10, 5), and the straight dock-to-dock line runs through the pond's center. Which equation describes the pond in center-radius form?

options.misconception: flips both signs when reading off the center
puts the radius where the squared radius belongs
takes the half-diameter as the center's x-coordinate

questions.explanation: The center of a circle is the midpoint of any diameter, so it is ((−2 + 10) / 2, (5 + 5) / 2) = (4, 5). That diameter spans 12 units, so the radius is 6 and r² = 36, giving (x − 4)² + (y − 5)² = 36. Flipping the signs moves the center to (−4, −5), writing 6 instead of 36 makes the pond six times too small in area, and 6 as a center confuses the radius with the center.
questions.hint: Average the two endpoints for the center, then square the half-span for the radius.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY

questions.learningObjective: count the crossings of a line with a circle using the center-to-line distance
questions.stem: A sprinkler wets a perfect circle of radius 17 meters centered at the origin of a coordinate plane. A straight fence runs along the line y = 8, parallel to the horizontal axis. How many points of the fence lie inside the wetted circle, and how long is the wetted stretch of fence?

options.misconception: reports the full diameter, as if the line ran through
claims tangency although the line misses the center
uses the 8-unit offset in place of the half-chord

questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the origin to the line y = 8 lands at (0, 8), 8 meters from the center, and 8 < 17, so the line cuts the circle twice. The half-chord along the fence is √(17² − 8²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15, so the wetted stretch runs from (−15, 8) to (15, 8), 30 meters long. A 34-meter stretch needs the fence through the center, one point needs the distance to equal 17, and 16 is the offset, not the half-chord.
questions.hint: Drop a perpendicular from the center to the line, then find the half-chord.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY

questions.learningObjective: find the area remaining after a circular island is removed from a pond
questions.stem: A circular fountain basin of radius 12 meters holds a circular island of radius 5 meters exactly at its center, and the rest is open water. What is the area of the open water, in square meters?

options.misconception: adds the island's area to the basin's area
ignores the island and uses the whole basin
divides out the pi factor as if given a scale

questions.explanation: Open water is the basin's disk minus the island's disk: π × 12² − π × 5² = 144π − 25π = 119π square meters, about 373.8. Adding instead gives 169π, which treats the island as extra water, and 144π forgets the island is there at all. Cancelling π would be right for a scale factor, but 12 and 5 are lengths in meters, so π stays in the answer.
questions.hint: Two areas, one subtracted from the other, both using πr squared.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY

questions.learningObjective: find the length of a chord cut by a segment between two points of a circle
questions.stem: A circular sign is described by (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 25. Two stakes are driven at (−6, 2) and (−1, 7), and a taut cable is strung straight between them across the sign's face. How long is the cable that lies inside the circle?

options.misconception: reports the diameter, which needs a chord through the center
reports the radius read off the equation
doubles each leg before combining the two runs

questions.explanation: The center is (−1, 2) with radius 5, and both stakes lie on the circle: (−6 + 1)² + (2 − 2)² = 25 and (−1 + 1)² + (7 − 2)² = 25. The cable runs from (−6, 2) to (−1, 7), so its length is √(5² + 5²) = √50 = 5√2 meters, about 7.07. The 90-degree central angle confirms it, since a chord spanning 90 degrees is 2r sin 45 degrees = 5√2 as well. Ten meters needs a chord through the center, 5 meters is only the radius, and 10√2 meters doubles each leg before adding.
questions.hint: Confirm both stakes satisfy the equation, then measure the straight run between them.
